purpose: Provides deterministic protocol peers for cross-platform host-client unit tests.
behavior: Uses real Unix socketpairs or Windows named pipes while the peer controls Ready, Spawned and arbitrary encoded replies.

The Mode::Pipe fixture uses three stdio pipes; its Mode::Pty variant sends no child stdio descriptors or handles with Spawn. Both use explicit environment and 1500 ms grace; bounded block() runs futures on a caller runtime separate from the library runtime.
Unix peers carry SCM_RIGHTS descriptors; Windows peers duplicate a real current-process handle for transfer tests.
contracts: Healthy request bound is 5 s and async test bound 20 s; malformed client frames panic the test.
dependencies: client platform Chan implementations and omni-proto codec are used directly.
failures_or_limits: The peer substitutes for the supervisor and does not execute requested fixture commands.

purpose: Covers Unix descriptor transfer, PTY release handshake, fork refusal and channel latency.
behavior: A large Spawn must carry exactly three descriptors once in stdin/stdout/stderr order; merged output with closed stdin carries only stdout.
PTY input duplicates the master; Go synchronously reports exec success/failure. A forked client must refuse every operation and emit no frame.
Stray descriptors kill the generation; K4 compares best interleaved p50 batches with a raw socket ping-pong baseline.
contracts: Linux release budget is max(200 microseconds, 3x bare); other builds use max(5 ms, 10x bare).
dependencies: client/unix.rs handles SCM_RIGHTS; client/hold.rs coordinates Go.
failures_or_limits: The performance case measures protocol round trips with a fake supervisor, not process execution latency.

purpose: Tests Windows bootstrap isolation, named-pipe identity and bounded supervisor termination.
behavior: Plants an inheritable host handle, starts an Omni helper and a std control, and compares actual object handles while both helpers remain alive.
Requires no inherited planted handle in the Omni helper, a visible one in the control, noninheritable bootstrap handles and a single pipe instance.
Rejects a connecting PID other than the started one; an unreleased helper must terminate only after its cooperative window.
contracts: Named events synchronize helpers; helper liveness is checked to prevent vacuous inheritance evidence.
failures_or_limits: Ignored idle_child is a subprocess role; source describes a mutation probe but no probe or Windows test ran here.

purpose: Implements Unix host socket transport, pipe creation and supervisor bootstrap.
behavior: Starts supervisor with control socket on stdin, null stdout/stderr and a separate process group after preparing its reaper/watch.
Sends descriptors by SCM_RIGHTS once; EMSGSIZE retries descriptor transfer with one byte; receives reject control-buffer truncation and set close-on-exec.
Channel close shuts down both directions then schedules identity-based kill after the cooperative window; PTY output master is duplicated for input.
contracts: Linux pipe2 and MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC make descriptor inheritance atomic.
Unix PTY reply marker must be [1,0] with one received master.
dependencies: client/keeper.rs owns identity and reaping; Tokio owns nonblocking socket readiness.
failures_or_limits: macOS sets FD_CLOEXEC after creation/receipt, leaving the explicitly documented inheritance window.

purpose: Implements Windows host bootstrap with process-handle identity and noninheritable transfers.
behavior: Creates a first-instance local named pipe, starts supervisor with bInheritHandles FALSE and CREATE_NO_WINDOW, and accepts only its PID.
Duplicates child ends into supervisor without inheritance; rollback closes remote values. PTY ends are taken back with DUPLICATE_CLOSE_SOURCE.
Disconnect schedules termination through the retained process handle after a window, avoiding numeric-PID reuse.
contracts: Spawned terminal ends must be both nonzero or both zero; bootstrap arguments must be nonempty plain tokens.
dependencies: windows-sys supplies CreateProcessW and DuplicateHandle; Tokio supplies named-pipe readiness.
failures_or_limits: Pipe name uses two keyed standard-hasher outputs; this file declares unpredictability but provides no cryptographic proof.

evidence.quote:
// SAFETY: both strings are NUL-terminated and alive, `line` is writable as CreateProcessW requires, and
    // `si`/`pi` are valid. bInheritHandles = FALSE: the new process inherits no handle of the host (R7).
    let ok = unsafe {
        CreateProcessW(
            app.as_ptr(),
            line.as_mut_ptr(),
            null(),
            null(),
            FALSE,
            CREATE_NO_WINDOW,
            null(),

            &si,
            &mut pi,
        )

purpose: Centralizes shared error construction policy and message ownership.
behavior: Private constructors bind each message to its ErrorCode, with public option names shared by language bindings.
Declares append-only per-work-package message modules; common helpers create InvalidArgument, Io and stream labels.
Argument bodies and environment values are withheld; PATH/PATHEXT lookup diagnostics are the explicitly declared exception.
contracts: Diagnostics identify fields and offsets without echoing ordinary argument/environment values.
dependencies: error/mod.rs owns Error and ErrorCode; per-WP modules add constructors.
failures_or_limits: Policy is stated here; individual formatting sites still determine what is disclosed.

purpose: Defines validation, executable-resolution and cwd diagnostics with stable error categories.
behavior: InvalidArgument covers empty command, NUL fields (including nul_in_cwd), malformed env keys, drive_relative_command, PTY sides and numeric ranges.
NotFound distinguishes missing child PATH, unsuccessful search and explicit path lookup; it includes searched PATH/PATHEXT.

NotExecutable distinguishes directory, permission and unsupported Windows extension. lookup_failed returns Io for residual filesystem errors, apart from separately classified missing and permission cases; drive_relative_cwd and cwd resolution/access failures return InvalidCwd, while nul_in_cwd remains InvalidArgument.
contracts: NUL argument/value messages reveal field/index/offset but omit the secret-bearing value.
dependencies: spawn validation and resolution plus binding numeric checks call these constructors.
failures_or_limits: Messages are diagnostic intent, not evidence that a particular validation ran; raw OS errors may add platform text.

purpose: Names supervisor bootstrap, generation, admission and stdio failures for callers.
behavior: Most constructors produce Io with generation number, failed operation or resource boundary and an actionable recovery suggestion.
SpawnFailed preserves the translated error code and errno supplied by the caller.

Resize after observed exit is Closed. For a held Unix terminal, Go preserves the translated SpawnFailed code (NotFound in the supplied test); a subsequent exited() query reports Io, using terminal_never_started while the generation remains alive because no exit status exists.
contracts: Gone-generation text says later spawn creates a new supervisor; saturated admission advises retry after requests finish.
dependencies: client generation/start/platform code supplies operation-specific values.
failures_or_limits: Error wording cannot prove cleanup or restart happened; it reports the failure path chosen by implementation.

purpose: Provides process-layer misuse messages and the retained terminal-support placeholder.
behavior: spawn with pty set gives InvalidArgument directing callers to spawn_pty.
Writing without a piped stdin gives InvalidArgument naming Stdin::Pipe; terminal_unsupported returns Io with historical W12 wording.
contracts: Message constructors are append-only work-package-owned entries.
dependencies: process child/spawn paths consume misuse constructors; terminal support is implemented elsewhere.
failures_or_limits: The existence of terminal_unsupported does not establish terminal support is absent at this pin.

purpose: Defines cancellation, output-limit and PTY-input error messages.
behavior: Pre-start cancellation reports Aborted and that nothing ran; in-run cancellation reports stopped tree and attached partial result.
OutputLimit names the affected stream and configured byte cap, describes truncated per-stream results and suggests streamed spawn output.
PTY plus run input is InvalidArgument because terminal input lacks separate EOF.
contracts: Constructors only create errors; process::run attaches the collected result.
dependencies: process/run.rs and deadline cancellation paths select these messages.
failures_or_limits: The PTY-input guidance mentions spawn with pty, while public Rust launch is spawn_pty; readers should use the API-specific entrypoint.

purpose: Defines stream-consumer, pump and stdin diagnostics.
behavior: A second output/lines claim is InvalidArgument and explicitly says detach is permanent.
Reader failure and lost pre-collection bytes produce Io, distinguishing an incomplete run from successful output.
Closed stdin yields Closed with the closing cause; write failure and thread-start failure are Io.
contracts: Loss is reported as an error for collection rather than silently returning complete-looking bytes.
dependencies: io queue/output/collect/stdin implementations provide stream and failure context.
failures_or_limits: Messages classify failure and guide callers but do not themselves cancel pumps or stop trees.

purpose: Explains Windows verbatim-argument validation failures without exposing tail contents.
behavior: Rejects the option on Unix or together with normal argv; NUL diagnostics name the option and byte offset while withholding the argument tail.
Batch-file target refusal explains that the library will not silently introduce cmd.exe for a verbatim command.
contracts: All constructors return InvalidArgument; callers may explicitly select cmd.exe when they accept its parsing contract.
dependencies: spawn/validate.rs owns the verbatim option and resolved-target checks, orchestrated by spawn::prepare; spawn/resolve.rs supplies the resolved executable path.
failures_or_limits: Suggested command-line syntax is explanatory text, not an executed or sanitized command.

behavior: Empty supervisor path is InvalidArgument and directs caller to a full binary path or default addon-relative lookup.
A different path after startup is InvalidArgument and says configuration belongs before first run/spawn.
contracts: This file names the path but owns no global configuration state.
dependencies: client/start.rs invokes these constructors when configuring its shared slot.
failures_or_limits: The constructor alone does not validate filesystem existence or executable compatibility.

purpose: Defines the stable public error vocabulary and optional collected run result.
behavior: Nonexhaustive ErrorCode provides eight categories and fixed uppercase strings shared with other languages.
Error keeps a private code/message and optional boxed RunOutput; result() exposes partial collection for Aborted, OutputLimit or Io.
Display writes CODE: message and std::error::Error is implemented without a nested source chain.
contracts: New errors start without a result; only internal with_result attaches one.
dependencies: types::RunOutput supplies the result shape; private messages constructors bind semantic code/text.
failures_or_limits: Code stability does not promise stable OS-specific message fragments.
